data.title: Ukraine Says SpaceX Is Still Restricting Starlink Access Despite Trump's Claims
data.description:
Satellite internet provider SpaceX (SPCX) is still limiting Ukraine's use of its Starshield military communications system, despite President Donald Trump's claims that the service has been restored. According to CNBC, Ukrainian officials confirmed on Friday that drones traveling faster than 100 miles per hour continue to lose their internet connections. The restrictions have been disrupting military operations since mid-October and have caused Ukraine to search for alternative satellite networks.

Starshield is a military version of SpaceX's Starlink internet service. Ukraine uses the technology to communicate with drones during military operations, even when those drones are far from the people controlling them. However, when a drone goes faster than the speed limit that's imposed on the service, its satellite connection can suddenly stop working. That can prevent operators from controlling the aircraft or receiving information from it.

Dmitri Alperovitch, a national security expert, said that Ukraine has already lost drones because of the restrictions. He also said that its ability to attack Russian supply routes has been reduced.

Meanwhile, Trump claimed on Thursday that Musk had restored the service. On Friday, he denied speaking with Musk about the issue and said that he would contact him if the problems continued. Ukrainian officials insist that the restrictions remain in place.

Ukraine Struggling to Find Alternatives to SpaceX

The disruptions have exposed how much Ukraine depends on SpaceX for military communications. Although the country uses other satellite services, officials have struggled to find an alternative that offers similar capabilities.

That dependence also gives SpaceX an important role in government communications. In the third quarter, its satellite connectivity business generated $5.25 billion in revenue, an increase of 69% from a year earlier. Of that amount, $2.13 billion came from government and business customers, although SpaceX does not disclose how much Ukraine contributes.

Ukraine is now taking steps to develop satellite communications that it can control itself. On Thursday, Ukraine's Defense Ministry signed an agreement with Finnish satellite company ICEYE and telecommunications equipment maker Nokia (NOK) to look into building a Ukrainian-controlled satellite network.

The proposed system would give Ukraine control over its own satellites and related communications equipment. However, the companies have not announced a construction schedule or disclosed how much the project could cost.

data.title: Why Is Penny Stock Bolt Biotherapeutics (BOLT) Up 62% Today?
data.description:
Bolt Biotherapeutics (BOLT) stock soared 61.81% on Friday after the biotechnology company announced its acquisition of Prana Therapies alongside a private placement. Bolt Biotherapeutics noted that the acquisition was structured as a sign-and-close reverse merger. Under this, the companies will combine on a stock-for-stock basis.

The terms of the deal will have 430,746 shares of BOLT stock and 16,360.929 shares of the company's Series D non-voting convertible preferred stock exchanged for all shares of Prana Therapies. This will result in current BOLT shareholders owning 6.9% of the company, while Prana Therapies' equity holders will own 51.7% of the company. The remaining 41.4% will belong to investors of a private placement that will take place at the same time as the reverse merger.

Bolt Biotherapeutics Private Placement

As part of the merger agreement, Bolt Biotherapeutics will conduct a $120 million private placement. This money will be used to acquire 13,995.311 shares of Series D non-voting convertible preferred stock, which are convertible to 13,995,311 shares of BOLT stock. These shares will be purchased for $8,574.30 each.

Bolt Biotherapeutics said that it expects this private placement to close on Oct. 26, 2026. The company said it plans for the preferred stock to immediately convert and the warrants to be exercised afterward.

What Will Bolt Biotherapeutics Do After the Merger?

Once the merger is complete, Bolt Biotherapeutics intends to focus on the development of Prana Therapies' pipeline. That includes its proprietary INSPIRE platform. This is led by PRA-216, a novel IL-4Rα/TSLP bispecific antibody currently in Phase 2 development in asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and atopic dermatitis. There's also plans for a Phase 2 study using PRA-216 in eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE).

When the deal is complete, Sheila Gujrathi will join Bolt Biotherapeutics' leadership team as its chief strategy officer. She will also become a member of its board. Gujrathi is the founder of Prana Therapies and its former CEO.

data.title: Why Are Gold and Silver Down Today, 10/23/26?
data.description:
Both gold (XAUUSD) and silver (XAGUSD) are trading lower on Thursday with losses of 0.75% and 1.16%, respectively. The two precious metals continue to face pressure from rising oil prices, rate hike expectations, and Treasury yields.

Brent crude (BZ), the global oil benchmark, is up 2.7% to a five-month high of $116 per barrel. Elevated oil prices have boosted the odds of higher interest rates at the October 28 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. The odds of a 25-basis-point hike are at 10.5%, up from 5.5% a day ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Gold and Silver Face Pressure From Rising Rates

Higher rates weigh on gold and silver because they don't generate interest. In other words, the opportunity cost of holding the precious metals relative to interest-bearing assets, such as Treasuries, rises in correlation with higher rates.

data.title: Microsoft's MAI-DxO Beats Human Doctors Over Two to One in Diagnoses; Microsoft Stock (NASDAQ:MSFT) Notches Up
data.description:
Remember when everybody used to go on WebMD, and diagnose themselves as having a range of diseases, many of which they did not actually have? Tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) has apparently refined the process of using an artificial intelligence for medical diagnoses to the point where it is twice as good at making diagnoses as human doctors. Microsoft stock gained fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Microsoft has posted a 0.48% loss in its share price over the past year.

It's Never Lupus

Fans of the TV show House will catch that reference right away, but apparently, House's team would have done a lot better if it had the Microsoft AI Diagnostic Orchestrator (MAI-DxO) on its side. Reports note that the tool "substantially outperformed practicing generalist physicians" in terms of overall diagnostic accuracy while ordering fewer tests and procedures on the patients. Naturally, real-world use of such a tool would require clinical testing, but if the early results hold out into the larger tests, then we may be running all our medical diagnoses through AI soon.

Microsoft plans to start testing the system further at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston before the year is out. An early test—the results of which were posted in the New England Journal of Medicine—revealed that the MAI-DxO system had an 83.2% success rate for diagnostic accuracy. Generalist physicians with reference materials, meanwhile, could only pull off a 36.1% accuracy rate. Without the reference materials, that rate plunged to 22%.

It Can't Be That Expensive

Meanwhile, a former Microsoft executive is coming out and saying the projected prices on Project Helix are too high to be believed. Former staffer Mike Ybarra simply cannot swallow the proposition that Microsoft would ever charge between $1,200 and $1,800 for the Project Helix, as earlier reports projected. The biggest reason for his objection is simple: a marked lack of value.

Consoles are "mass-audience devices," Ybarra noted. Thus, they need to be able to reach the mass audience. A price tag like that simply prices out the mass audience. Thus, Ybarra noted, "A console at the prices rumored below will never sell meaningful units to be of any value vs. alternatives. Zero."

data.title: "Project Crystal Sun" Gets Approval in Texas, Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Slips
data.description:
Electric vehicle giant Tesla (TSLA) managed to get approval for its "Project Crystal Sun" initiative in Texas, as Fort Bend County commissioners offered up a slate of tax benefits for Tesla's planned solar cell factory. This is one of the last local approvals Tesla needed. Tesla will now determine where exactly to build its newest factory. Tesla shares still dropped fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Tesla stock has seen a 13.64% loss in its share price over the past year.

Spoiled for Choice

Reports suggest that Tesla would get a property tax abatement out of Fort Bend County, along with what was called a "Chapter 381 economic development agreement." Further, Tesla was in line to get a "…foreign trade zone non-objection," along with payments in lieu of certain taxes and a separate payment in lieu of taxes "true-up" agreement. A true-up is generally the difference between estimated payments—in this case tax payments–and actual payments taxes assessed.

Once the project goes live, Tesla will start building a factory that makes solar cells and finished modules. It is looking to do so on a parcel of land roughly 3,000 acres south of the Brazos River in Texas. The plant will handle every part of the process, starting with raw metal and going all the way through solar cell testing, reports note. The new plan offered does not necessarily mean that area will get the Tesla plant installed. It does increase the chances as Tesla now knows what the local government is willing to offer.

Promotion

Tesla Cameras Save the Day

We all know that Tesla cars come with an array of cameras, but many of us might not have expected Tesla cameras to serve as a way to protect a person against false allegations. This happened to a man named Kevin Finley in Seminole County, Florida, where a Tesla camera recorded video that led to him being found not guilty of charges in court.

Finley had been the subject of a traffic stop where he was alleged to have driven through an intersection at a high rate of speed. While he was never charged with felony fleeing and eluding, he was issued a set of citations for other charges. Finley asserted that he had not done any such thing and had the video to prove it. The officers at the time did not care, reports note. The video did, however, care and ultimately disproved several of the officers' allegations. One of the officers, Officer Erik Schwartz, was ultimately dismissed from his position as part of an investigation into the charges.

In addition, Iran has stepped up attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, further disrupting global energy supplies. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said that October has recorded more attacks on commercial ships in the strait than any month since March, when the war began.
